summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and hemorrhoids, was admitted with chest pain, abdominal pain, and gastrointestinal bleeding. He also reported hematuria and dysuria. Initial evaluation showed no acute cardiac ischemia, with normal troponins and ECGs. The GI bleed was attributed to hemorrhoids, with stable hemoglobin. Liver enzymes were elevated consistent with alcoholic hepatitis, improving during the stay. A urine analysis indicated a urinary tract infection, treated with ciprofloxacin, and a renal ultrasound revealed an enlarged prostate. The patient eloped before a scheduled echocardiogram but returned later to receive discharge instructions and prescriptions. He was discharged home with plans to follow up for cardiac testing, urology evaluation, and continuation of treatment for alcohol-related liver disease and infection.
